title: RegistryAuth asked per token request, not fixed at construction
why: ECR passwords expire after about 12 hours; a fixed field cannot be replaced, so expiry handling lives in one provider instead of every caller
alternative: Rebuild or mutate the store when credentials change - rejected: spreads expiry handling across fetch, push and train

intent: Hand-written SigV4 signer checked against AWS test vectors

title: SigV4 verified against AWS's published test suite, scoped to STS and ECR
why: A signer tested only against our own fake would agree with its own mistakes; AWS publishes expected signatures (get-vanilla, post-x-www-form-urlencoded) that fail on any canonicalisation or key-derivation bug. Scope is limited to a / path and simple queries, which is all STS and ECR need.
alternative: Round-trip test against a fake AWS endpoint only - rejected: cannot catch an error shared by signer and fake. Full SigV4 including S3 path rules - rejected: unused code in a startup tool

intent: IRSA web identity credentials, AWS endpoints and retrying AWS HTTP

title: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is not SigV4-signed
why: The service-account JWT is the proof of identity and STS validates it against the cluster's OIDC issuer; there are no AWS keys yet to sign with. Signing starts with the ECR call.
alternative: Sign the STS call - rejected: impossible, the keys are what this call returns

title: Re-read the web identity token file on every resolve
why: The kubelet rotates the projected JWT (about hourly); a cached copy would send an expired token on long train runs
alternative: Read once at startup - rejected: fails exactly on long runs

title: Retry transient AWS failures, surface 4xx immediately
why: Connection errors, 429 and 5xx are transient; AccessDenied and expired tokens are answers, and retrying them only delays the error and loads STS. Errors carry AWS's message, never tokens or keys.
alternative: Retry everything - rejected: masks denials, slows failing starts. No retries - rejected: one STS blip would drop a pod's cache

title: Ask STS for JSON instead of parsing XML
why: Accept: application/json avoids an XML parser (secure parsing is its own risk surface) in a dependency-free core. Verified against a fake only; to confirm on real STS in the end-to-end check.
alternative: Parse the default XML response - rejected: more code and XXE-hardening for no gain

intent: ECR registry auth, mid-run refresh, environment selection and docs

title: Cache the ECR login until 5 minutes before expiry and never hand out an expired one
why: A token about to die could expire between being handed out and used; refreshing early removes the race, and a failed refresh throws instead of returning the stale login
alternative: Refresh only after a 401 - rejected: every long run would take at least one avoidable failure

title: Retry once after a 401 on an authenticated request, only if the provider returns a different login
why: An ECR login can expire mid-run; invalidating and re-asking recovers it. If the provider returns the same login the refusal is real, so we stop instead of looping.
alternative: Never retry - rejected: long train runs fail at the 12 h mark. Retry unconditionally - rejected: hides a real permission error behind extra requests

title: A Docker-config entry wins; ECR is used only for an ECR host with a pod web identity
why: Existing static authentication must keep working unchanged, and a non-ECR registry must never trigger AWS calls or token-file reads
alternative: ECR first when env is present - rejected: surprises users who set an explicit secret. Always try AWS - rejected: extra network calls on every other registry

title: Second role is an environment variable, not a new flag
why: The role differs per container (fetch vs trainer) and is set by deployment config; an env var fits Helm and the injector without widening three subcommands' CLI surface
alternative: --aws-role-arn flag on push, fetch and train - rejected: three places to document and test for the same setting
